Decision — Email never creates HTML

Status: accepted 2026-10-27.

The decision

  • Email sends text/plain only. The body is written in Markdown and goes out as that Markdown text, text/plain; charset=utf-8. Files are attached as their own parts under multipart/mixed.
  • No HTML part is ever generated. Email does not render Markdown to HTML, and does not add a multipart/alternative HTML version, a stylesheet, inline images by cid:, tracking pixels or scripts.
  • A recipient without a Markdown-aware reader sees plain text. That is intended. Markdown is readable as written.
  • This is a security choice, not a gap. Do not add "HTML convenience", an HTML toggle, a rich-text composer, or a Markdown-to-HTML step to the send path. A change of this decision needs a new decision.

Why

  • HTML mail carries markup, CSS and sometimes script. Each is an attack surface for the reader at the other end, and a body that can be altered while it is relayed over SMTP between servers.
  • Plain text has none of that. What the sender wrote is what is delivered, and any reader can show it safely.
  • Markdown keeps the structure people want (headings, lists, links, code) without needing HTML to show it.

What stays

  • Reading HTML mail. Email still receives HTML mail from other clients. It shows the plain-text part first and prints any HTML as text. Nothing from a received email runs or loads.
  • Attachments. A user may attach an .html file like any other file. It travels as an attachment, not as the message body.
